tokyo_gusuku.price_note: Full menu with prices, read from the shop’s own site — starters, chanpuru, goat dishes, fried items, single plates, rice and noodles, and the drinks list including the awamori bottles. 新宿区新宿3-8-5 中川ビル2F, 19:00–02:00, open every day, one minute from Shinjuku-sanchome C4; the shop states an average spend of about ¥7,000. Tabelog is UNVERIFIED rather than empty: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT ON THIS RECORD, AND ONE OF THE SHARPEST TRAPS IN THE WHOLE DATASET: 沖縄そば CONTAINS NO BUCKWHEAT AT ALL. It is made from 100% WHEAT flour, and it is permitted to keep the word そば only by a specific exemption negotiated with Japan’s fair-trade authorities — every other noodle sold as そば must contain at least 30% buckwheat. So a coeliac who has learned to be wary of soba for the usual reason (二八, 打ち粉, shared water) will still be wrong here, and wrong in the opposite direction: this is not soba with some wheat in it, it is a wheat noodle wearing the name. It appears twice on this menu, as a bowl and as ゴーヤめし’s companion. ⚠ THE SECOND TRAP IS 麸 AND IT RUNS THE OTHER WAY. フーチャンプルー is built on 麸 — FU, which is pure WHEAT GLUTEN, the most concentrated wheat product in Japanese cooking — and yet fu is entirely plant-based, so a vegan scanning for a tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry may land on precisely the dish a coeliac must avoid most. The two diets fail on opposite halves of this menu repeatedly. ⚠ AND ソーミンチャンプルー IS SOMEN: wheat noodles, stir-fried. Three of the nine noodle-or-gluten items here hide their wheat behind an Okinawan word. ⚠ WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD HERE, AND IT IS MORE THAN MOST: ジーマミ豆腐 is not tofu at all but PEANUT and sweet-potato starch — no soy, no wheat, no dashi, and a nut allergen instead. 豆腐よう is island tofu fermented in 紅麹 and AWAMORI, which is rice-based. スヌイ is Okinawan mozuku seaweed. ゴーヤ刺し is raw bitter melon. And the awamori list matters for a coeliac beyond this shop: awamori is distilled from long-grain RICE with black koji and never from barley, which makes it the one Japanese spirit category with no grain question at all — unlike 麦焼酎, and unlike whisky. ⚠ ONE ITEM IS A DELIBERATE-LOOKING VEGAN TRAP: スク豆腐 is chilled island tofu with スク on top — salted juvenile RABBITFISH. A tofu dish that is a fish dish, with nothing in the Japanese name to say so unless you know the word.

items.note: ⚠ 油みそ / アンダンスー IS NOT A VEGETABLE DIP. It is MISO cooked down with PORK BELLY and fat — the cucumber is the vehicle. Miso is also frequently 麦味噌, barley.
Sliced pig ear cartilage. The 酢みそ dressing is miso and vinegar, and miso is fermented on koji that is often barley.
Jellyfish is animal; a ume dressing is normally soy-based.

⚠ A REAL FIND, AND WORTH KNOWING WHAT IT IS: island tofu fermented for months in 紅麹 red koji and AWAMORI, eaten in tiny slivers like a cheese. Soybeans, rice koji and rice spirit — nothing animal at any point, and no wheat unless the koji is a barley one, which for tofuyo it traditionally is not. One of the few Japanese fermented delicacies that reaches a vegan.

⚠ IT IS NOT TOFU AND IT IS NOT SOY. ジーマミ is Okinawan for PEANUT: this is peanut milk set with sweet-potato starch, which makes it naturally free of wheat and of anything animal — and a NUT dish, which matters more here than either diet flag. The gluten question is only the sauce poured over it, which is normally a soy-based one; ask for it plain.

Island tofu is firmer and saltier than mainland tofu, coagulated with seawater. Plant in itself; it arrives with soy sauce, and chilled tofu in Japan very often carries a pinch of KATSUOBUSHI as a garnish nobody mentions.

The signature Okinawan stir-fry: bitter melon, island tofu, pork and egg. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

⚠ THE MOST CONCENTRATED WHEAT ITEM ON THIS MENU AND IT LOOKS LIKE THE VEGETARIAN ONE. 麸 (fu) is PURE WHEAT GLUTEN — flour washed until only the protein remains — so this dish is closer to eating gluten neat than any noodle is. It is also entirely plant-based in itself, which is exactly the problem: a vegan scanning an Okinawan menu for a tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry can land on the single worst dish here for a coeliac. Deep-fried island tofu — plant in itself, and the best-looking vegan prospect in this section. Two things stop it: it comes out of the same fryer as the panko croquettes above, and atsuage is normally served with soy sauce and very often a scattering of KATSUOBUSHI.

items.ja: スヌイ沖縄県産もずく
items.note: ⚠ ONE OF THE BEST VEGAN ITEMS HERE. スヌイ is the Okinawan word for mozuku, a fine seaweed harvested in the islands — plant, and nothing else in the bowl. The gluten flag is against only because mozuku is served in 三杯酢, a vinegar dressing built on SOY SAUCE and usually dashi; ask for it with plain vinegar and it clears both.

items.en: Island tofu topped with salted juvenile rabbitfish
items.note: ⚠ THE PUREST VEGAN TRAP ON THIS MENU. It reads as a tofu dish and the whole point of it is the スク — salted juvenile RABBITFISH, laid across the top. Nothing in the name says fish unless you already know the Okinawan word, and the fish is the dish rather than a garnish. Soy sauce as well.
Pork belly simmered for hours in AWAMORI, soy sauce and brown sugar. The soy is dissolved through the meat, so there is no plain version.
Pig trotters, soy-simmered.
SPAM and fried egg — the Okinawan staple. Luncheon meat commonly carries wheat starch as a binder, which is the open question.
SPAM, fried crisp.

⚠ ONE OF VERY FEW HOT-KITCHEN-FREE PLANT DISHES IN THIS DATASET: raw bitter melon, sliced. No stir-fry, no egg, no pork, no fryer. The gluten flag is a question only because 刺し in Japan means "with soy sauce" by default — ask for salt instead.

⚠ WORTH NOTING FOR THE METHOD: スーチカー is pork preserved in SALT rather than soy, which is unusual on a Japanese board and removes the obvious wheat route. Pork, and the finishing seasoning is not described.

⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE LINE ON THIS RECORD: OKINAWA SOBA CONTAINS NO BUCKWHEAT WHATSOEVER. It is 100% WHEAT flour, kneaded with lye water, and it keeps the word そば only through a specific exemption from Japan’s labelling rules — every other product sold as そば must be at least 30% buckwheat. A coeliac who has learned that soba is risky because of 二八 blends and shared 打ち粉 will still get this one wrong, because there is no buckwheat to dilute: it is a wheat noodle with a soba name. The broth is pork and katsuo, and it is topped with 三枚肉 simmered in soy.

items.ja: やきそば（ソース／しょうゆ／けちゃっぷ／イカスミ）
items.note: ⚠ ALSO NOT BUCKWHEAT. Yakisoba noodles are WHEAT, and the shop offers four sauces of which three are wheat routes in their own right: ソース is a Worcester-style sauce, しょうゆ is soy, and ケチャップ is the only one that is not. Squid ink is the fourth.
Rice cooked or fried with bitter melon — the rice is clean, but a ゴーヤめし in an Okinawan kitchen normally includes pork or luncheon meat and is soy-seasoned.
Okinawa’s own beer, and BEER IS BARLEY MALT — gluten from the grain itself. The only beer on the list.

items.price: ボトル 5,000円 / グラス 700円
items.note: ⚠ AWAMORI IS THE CLEANEST SPIRIT CATEGORY IN JAPAN FOR A COELIAC, and it is worth understanding why rather than just noting it. Awamori is distilled from long-grain INDICA RICE using BLACK KOJI (黒麹) — rice and rice only, never barley, unlike 麦焼酎 and unlike whisky, and unlike the soba shochu recorded elsewhere in this dataset whose koji is often barley. There is no grain question to ask about any bottle on this list.
Aged awamori — rice and black koji.

tokyo_texmex_factory_shibuya_k.price_note: Full food menu with prices, tax included, read from the shop’s own official お料理 page — starters, platillos, salads, tacos, burritos, sliders, fajitas, sides and desserts. The course, drinks and lunch pages exist and are not itemised here. 渋谷区神南1-19-3 ハイマンテン神南ビル2F, five minutes from Shibuya; 109 seats; open 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:30 on weekdays, through the day at weekends. A TABLE CHARGE of ¥330 per person applies after 15:00 on weekdays and all day at weekends. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge. ⚠ MEXICAN FOOD HAS A REPUTATION AS THE SAFE CUISINE FOR A COELIAC, BECAUSE CORN IS NOT WHEAT. That reputation is worth exactly as much as the tortilla it is built on, and THIS MENU NEVER SAYS WHICH TORTILLA IT USES. Corn tortillas and flour tortillas both appear across Tex-Mex; burritos are conventionally flour, tacos conventionally corn, and the shop’s ピンクタコス are coloured, which says nothing about the grain. Not one item description names the flour. So the single question that decides most of this board is the one to ask at the door, and no amount of reading resolves it here. ⚠ THE FRYER IS SHARED AND DEMONSTRABLY CARRIES TORTILLA: チミチャンガ is a tortilla-wrapped parcel deep-fried, and フライドチーズケーキ is a cheesecake wrapped in a large tortilla and deep-fried. If those tortillas are flour, then the chips, the shrimp fry, the jalapeño bombs and the chicken are all shared-oil problems. ⚠ THE SHOP DOES OFFER A REAL PLANT OPTION AND SAYS SO PLAINLY: ベジタブルミート, described as ダイズを主原料とした「ソイミート」— soy protein — available as a ¥490 taco, a ¥1,410 burrito and in the タコスサラダボウル. That is an explicit meat substitute rather than a dish that happens to lack meat, which is rare in this dataset. What it does not tell you is whether cheese and sour cream come with it as standard; on this menu they usually do. パクチビーンズ, ワカモレ and the vegetable fajita are the other plant routes. ⚠ AND THE ONE DISH WITH NO TORTILLA ANYWHERE NEAR IT IS SAUCED WITH SOY. The ¥4,880 メキシカン ビーフステーキ is finished with しょう油ベースのオリジナルステーキソース — a SOY SAUCE-based steak sauce, in a Mexican restaurant, stated in the shop’s own description. The steak is the obvious coeliac order here and the sauce is a Japanese wheat route that nothing about the cuisine would lead anyone to expect. Ask for it plain.

items.note: The shop lists it as chips baked with cheese under sour cream sauce, chilli meat, avocado, pico de gallo and coriander. A stewed chilli is one of the few Tex-Mex dishes with no tortilla in it at all, and this kitchen serves it with wheat bread instead. Ask whether it can come without.

tokyo_koishitai_tai_tantanmen_.price_note: Full menu with prices, read from the shop’s own site — ramen, lunch sets, combo sets, seasonal bowls, rice dishes and the topping list. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. The shop describes its owner as having trained for fourteen years in FRENCH cooking before opening a 鯛担麺専門店, and it uses Ehime sea bream throughout. ⚠ THIS RECORD IS ENTIRELY CLOSED ON BOTH AXES AND THE REASONS ARE WORTH SEPARATING. For a coeliac: every bowl is a wheat noodle, the shop offers no alternative, and the two 担麺 bowls add a second wheat route on top — a Japanese tantan sauce is sesame paste let down with SOY, and Chinese fermented pastes are made with wheat flour besides. For a vegan: the entire shop is built on sea bream. 鯛出汁 is not a seasoning here, it is the concept — it is in the broth, in the rice, in the marinated egg, and sold on its own at ¥100 as a topping. ⚠ THE ONE STRUCTURAL POINT WORTH CARRYING AWAY IS ABOUT 鯛めし. Sea bream rice at ¥250 is the only substantial item here that is not made of wheat, and a coeliac travelling with other people could in principle eat it while they have ramen. It is still not safe as published: 鯛めし is rice cooked in the bream dashi, and a Japanese kitchen’s dashi is normally 白だし or だし醤油 — soy, and therefore wheat. So the rice is the thing to ask about, not the thing to assume. ⚠ AND ONE NAME NOT TO MISREAD: 鯛塩濃厚そば. The そば here means RAMEN in the 中華そば sense, not buckwheat — the same misreading this dataset keeps meeting. What 塩 does tell you is real, though: that bowl is seasoned with SALT rather than a soy tare, which removes one wheat route while leaving the noodle. It is the closest thing on this menu to a considered order, and it is still a wheat bowl.

items.note: ⚠ THE SHOP’S SIGNATURE AND A DOUBLE WHEAT ROUTE. Heat is chosen from 0 to 3, with a 激辛 level at ¥50 more. The broth is built on 鯛, SEA BREAM from Ehime, so every bowl here is fish. ⚠ The noodles are WHEAT — the shop has them made to its own specification, with the thickness varying by bowl, which is a statement about texture and not about grain.

tokyo_ore_no_kappo_robata_shin.price_note: ⚠ NO ITEMS RECORDED, AND THE REASON IS A HALF-SUCCESS RATHER THAN A DEAD END. The shop publishes its menu as a 1.2MB PDF, which was downloaded and extracted. The PDF is BILINGUAL, and exactly half of it survived: every English dish name came through, while the Japanese names AND EVERY PRICE are set in Adobe-Japan1 CID fonts that the extractor cannot resolve — it reports Unknown character collection for each. So what is recoverable is an English dish list with no prices and no Japanese. That is not enough to write items with: this dataset’s ja field is what a diner points at in a Japanese restaurant, and filling it with English would produce a card that is useless at the counter, while inventing the Japanese from an English translation would be fabrication. The English list is therefore recorded here as prose, and the item list is left empty until a readable menu appears. Tabelog is UNVERIFIED rather than empty: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ WHAT THE ENGLISH SIDE OF THE PDF NAMES, verbatim, as orientation only: under Signature Fish & Seafood — Jumbo Prawn, Premium Sardine, Whole Atka Mackerel, Half Atka Mackerel, Charcoal-Grilled Semi-Dried Squid, Whole Golden Eye Snapper Char-Grilled. Under Signature Meat — Robata-Grilled Ezo Venison, Charcoal-Grilled Lamb, Charcoal-Grilled Thick-Cut Beef Tongue, Charcoal-Grilled Tokyo Wagyu Misuji (Chuck Flap), Chef’s Selection Charcoal-Grilled Wagyu Beef. Under Vegetables — Charcoal-Grilled Potatoes, Awajishima Sweet Onion, Seared Tomato. Sashimi — Assorted Sashimi, priced for two with an additional-person supplement. Appetizers and Cold Dishes — Horse Meat Yukhoe, ORENO Seasonal Seafood Salad, Yukhoe, Salted Squid (Shiokara) from Hokkaido, Sous-Vide Chicken Liver, Salted Sea Pineapple from Hokkaido, House-Smoked Cream Cheese, Assorted Pickles, Shark Cartilage with Ume Plum Sauce. Hot Appetizers — Deep-Fried Whole Prawn with Head, Fried Scallops, Avocado Tempura Fritter. Rice and Soup — Donabe Rice with Snow Crab and Salmon Roe, Donabe Rice with Isshiki Eel and Salmon Roe, Seared Mackerel Sushi, Aka Dashi (Red Miso Soup), with Extra Salmon Roe as a supplement. Desserts — Robata-Roasted Sweet Potato with Ice Cream, Brown Sugar Ice Cream, Hojicha Jelly with Condensed Milk Sauce. ⚠ WHY THAT LIST IS WORTH KEEPING EVEN UNPRICED: a ROBATA GRILL is structurally one of the better formats for a coeliac, because charcoal-grilled fish, meat and vegetables are food, fire and salt with nothing to hide behind — and this board is dominated by whole grilled fish, grilled meat and three grilled vegetables. The questions are narrow and askable: whether each item is finished with a soy TARE or with salt, and what the tempura fritter and the two deep-fried items share for oil (the Avocado Tempura Fritter is wheat batter outright, and 赤だし miso soup is fermented on koji that may be barley). For a vegan the three grilled vegetables and the pickles are the whole board, and even those need the tare question asked. None of this is verified for this kitchen; it is the shape of the questions, not the answers.

tokyo_jimbocho_shokuniku_cente.price_note: No dish and no price. The shop has a first-party site with a page headed メニュー, which was fetched and read: it is a hub of brand copy and links rather than a menu, and the per-branch MENU links it offers lead to an anchor on the store page, which was also fetched. That store page carries no items either — its images have no alt text and nothing but a title graphic is named. So the menu is signposted throughout the site and published nowhere on it. ⚠ NOTE ON ACCESS FOR FUTURE TICKS: this site is served over plain HTTP and its HTTPS certificate does not match the hostname — it presents a shared *.sakura.ne.jp certificate — so any fetcher that upgrades HTTP to HTTPS fails on a certificate error rather than a 404. It has to be read over http:// explicitly. Tabelog is UNVERIFIED rather than empty: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ THE ONLY FIGURES PUBLISHED ARE BUDGETS, and they are recorded here rather than as items because they are not dishes: an average spend of ¥2,500, or ¥3,000 for a party booking, and a notice dated December 2024 announcing that LUNCH would rise to ¥1,250 from January 2025. 千代田区神田神保町2-16. ⚠ WHAT THE SITE DOES ESTABLISH ABOUT THE FORMAT: it is a 焼肉・ホルモン専門店 — a yakiniku and OFFAL specialist — operated directly by a meat wholesaler, claiming 100％国産肉 and naming its own brands 上州牛, 上州豚 and 上州豚とことん, the last raised on feed containing plum extract. That is provenance, not preparation, and it says nothing about either diet. ⚠ NOTHING ABOUT WHAT REACHES THE PLATE IS RECORDED, deliberately. The question at any yakiniku is タレ or 塩 — a soy-based dipping and marinating sauce against plain salt — and it is unanswerable from this site. A vegan has nothing to work with at an offal specialist. Re-check if the operator ever publishes the per-branch menu the site keeps linking to.
